transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, um… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting a little too caught up in how I look, especially now that I’m more in front of people for work. I plan events, so there are more photos and meeting people, and I keep noticing this one part of my face that looks uneven to me in pictures. 

Other people say they can barely see it, so I know it probably sounds small, but I can’t really stop staring at it once I notice it. I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets… I don’t know, more in my head.
Can you tell me if this concern about your appearance has been affecting your ability to do your job or causing you a lot of emotional distress?

Um… yeah, a little. I mean, I’m still getting my work done, mostly, but it has slowed me down more than I’d like to admit.

There was one planning deadline where I missed part of it because I kept getting stuck on how I looked in the event materials, like photos and things going out. And now even normal stuff, like vendor calls or prepping for meetings, takes longer than it should because I’m trying to make sure I look okay first. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, but it’s been stressful.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms specifically revolve around preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance that causes significant distress and impairment in functioning, which is most consistent with Body dysmorphic disorder. Other disorders are less likely given the specificity of the concern and the nature of the impairment described.
